stories.title: Game #16 Preview & Open Thread: Sabres vs Blue Jackets
stories.summary:
Buffalo in a special Hockey Fights Cancer Night event partnering with Roswell Park



Buffalo Sabres (7-5-3) vs Columbus Blue Jackets (7-7-0)



Puck Drop: 7:00 pm ET | KeyBank Center, Buffalo NY



TV: MSG-B, ESPN+, Fubo, Hulu + Live TV



Radio: WGR 550, Sirius XM (app)



Know Your Opponent



Columbus Blue Jackets



Record: 7-7-0 | 14 PTS



Last Game: 2-1 shootout win against Dallas Stars



Division Ranking: Metropolitan 6th



PP: 28th, 16.2% (6/37) [Sabres: 27th, 16.3% (8/49)]



PK: 24th, 73.2% (30/41) [Sabres: 27th, 69.8% (37/53)]



Season Series: Sabres 0-1-0 Blue Jackets this season



What to Watch



1. Playing With A Lead



When they started their West Coast swing last week, Buffalo had some atrocious record of playing either level or from behind for nearly 80% of their ice time. That got marginally better as they went three-for-three in California but then in a tight division game two nights ago at home against division rivals Ottawa Senators, the Sabres led going into the third period but failed to score a killer second goal. They ended up on the wrong side of a 2-1 scoreline after being outskated by the Sens in the final stanza, to Lindy Ruff’s chagrin. 



Granted this is a young side and needs to develop some maturity and character, but just last season we were seeing a deluge of empty net goals as Buffalo closed out wins with aplomb, and we’re not quite seeing that mental fortitude yet this season. 



2. Line Blender Is Back



The revolving door in and out of the medical area at KeyBank Center has meant that the Sabres haven’t had a settled lineup in recent games. Add to that the brutal (lack of) form for a few players and that means we’re going to see some new combinations again tonight. 



The biggest of those will be Ryan McLeod sitting up in the box seats tonight, and he understands why he’s going to be there too – “Obviously it’s frustrating being out of the lineup, without the team, helping out, but it’s just kind of getting back to the basics. They could tell I was struggling, and it’s kind of a bit of a fresh start.”



Somehow Josh Norris keeps his spot in the squad, bizarrely enough. Jiri Kulich is seeing some reps with the power play unit while Josh Doan has been added to the penalty kill group. On defense, Louis Crevier is getting a break as well with Conor Timmins healthy again.  



3. Kolumbus Kryptonite



There is something about Columbus that always matches up really well for the Ohio side against Buffalo. Over the last five years the Sabres are only 6-8-2 against the Blue Jackets and seem to fail more often than they should against the Columbus team. 



General Manager Jarmo Kekäläinen ended his 11-year stint with Columbus in early 2024 and has been with the Sabres since the spring of 2025. Prying the Finn away hasn’t done much to change that record, but hopefully he ends up making the Sabres as difficult to play against for everyone as Columbus are for Buffalo. 



Ex-Leaf Matthew Knies feasted on the Sabres in the season opener as Columbus won 6-3, and Kent Johnson and Zach Werenski always seem to score against Buffalo too.

stories.title: SSFC Spotlight: Trinity Byars finding the back of the net
Sabres squander late lead in 2-1 home loss to Senators
stories.summary:
New jerseys, same problems for Buffalo 



Box score



Score: Ottawa Senators 2, Buffalo Sabres 1Shots: Ottawa 30, Buffalo 25



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Peyton Krebs 1 (Thompson, Benson)Ottawa Senators Goals: Shane Pinto 6 (Tomasino, Chabot), Michael Amadio 5 (Stutzle, Zetterlund) 



Quick Thoughts



First Period – Sluggish start



Colten Ellis got the game off to an electrifying start, flashing the pad to absolutely rob Ottawa’s Michael Amadio on a one-timer less than two minutes in.



It took Buffalo a while to get their legs moving, which is somewhat understandable considering their return from the west coast and three days between games. Ottawa had the majority of the early chances during the first 10 minutes of the period, but thanks to Ellis, the game remained 0-0.



The first extended Sabres spell in the offensive zone came after the second TV timeout, when the Quinn-Ostlund-Doan line won a couple puck battles and mustered two shots on net, including a deflected shot on the doorstep by Ostlund that required a good save by Senators goalie Samuel Ersson. Shortly after, Tage Thompson had a great look in the slot, but again, Ersson made the stop.



With just over three minutes to play in the period, a turnover by Jason Zucker in the offensive zone sprung Ottawa on a 3-on-1, but Nick Cousins’ shot missed the net. Mattias Samuelsson then made a strong defensive play to break up a partial 2-on-1 a minute later.



The Sabres needed Ellis to be sharp early and often in the first period while they found their footing in the game, and fortunately, he was, which kept the game scoreless after one.



Second Period – Krebs opens the scoring



Jason Zucker had a good opportunity about two minutes into the period, as he took a cross-ice pass in stride and ripped a wrist shot from the right face-off circle, but Ersson managed to keep the puck out while Josh Norris was just beaten to the rebound.



Ottawa went to the game’s first power play with 13:56 to play in the second, when Rasmus Dahlin took a holding penalty to prevent a Tim Stutzle breakaway. In a battle of poor special teams, it was Buffalo’s lowly penalty kill that prevailed to kill off the minor, holding Ottawa without a quality scoring chance.



Buffalo conceded another 2-on-1 rush with seven minutes remaining in the period, but the pass across to an open Senator missed the mark.



Finally, the deadlock was broken by Peyton Krebs’ first goal of the season.



Zach Benson managed to control a loose puck among a crowd in front of the net, and neatly backhanded a pass to the high slot for Tage Thompson, who ripped a shot that was deflected by Krebs past Ersson to give the Sabres a 1-0 lead with six minutes exactly remaining in the period. 



Ottawa had a great chance to respond with a power play shortly after Krebs’ opener, but it was Ellis to the rescue once again. The 26-year-old pushed across to stop a one-time effort from Drake Batherson, before emulating Dominik Hasek with a sprawling blocker save to keep out a Tim Stutzle rebound. 



Buffalo managed to kill off the rest of the Senators’ man advantage, and take a 1-0 lead into the third period.



Third Period – Blown opportunity



The Sabres had an early power play opportunity to extend their lead, with their best chance coming when Tage Thompson faked everyone out with a pass to Jack Quinn for a one-timer, but the winger fanned on the shot with an open net in front of him.



Josh Doan drew another Ottawa penalty a few minutes later, winning a race to prevent an icing before being boarded by Jordan Spence. However, Buffalo again failed to take advantage, and it wasn’t long before they were burned for it.



A tired Sabres forward group iced the puck, and the Senators won the ensuing faceoff cleanly to set up Philip Tomasino with a clean look in the slot. Ellis made the initial save, but overcommitted on the push across. It left an open net and rebound for Shane Pinto, who wasn’t tied up by Ryan McLeod, to bury. Buffalo was doing a good job slowing the game down prior to that sequence, but all of a sudden were in a 1-1 game with 8:27 remaining in the third.



The Senators’ goal shifted the momentum, and Ottawa turned things around completely with just over three minutes to play.



The Senators won the puck while the Benson-Ostlund-Doan line was forechecking, and managed to chip it past Dahlin who was caught pinching, igniting an odd-man rush the other way. Ostlund did a good job getting back to defend, but couldn’t take away the cross-ice pass from Stutzle to Amadio, who avenged his missed chance in the first period by beating a sprawling Ellis to put Ottawa up 2-1 late.



Buffalo pulled the goalie with just about a minute and a half to go, but couldn’t tie the game despite having a couple decent looks, dropping a tough one against a division opponent on home ice.



Quick Thoughts



Simply put: the Sabres cannot afford to lose a divisional game like that in regulation with how competitive the Atlantic is.



Ellis was sharp and gave Buffalo a golden opportunity to take two points from Ottawa, but failed to do so thanks to a couple defensive lapses late in the third period. At minimum, the Sabres should be getting a point in this game, but instead leave empty-handed.



The Sabres were horrendous in the faceoff circle, and other than the Benson-Ostlund-Doan line, failed to produce much of anything at 5-on-5 — albeit against a sound defensive team. 



The other storyline here is yet another lackluster performance on home ice, a trend that dates back to last year’s postseason and seems to be continuing early this campaign. It’s only game 15, and there’s plenty of season left, but Buffalo will need to sort out its home form to stay afloat in the Atlantic.



But, at the least the Hometown Remix jerseys looked cool.



Next Up



The Sabres continue their four-game homestand on Friday against Columbus, with puck drop set for 7 p.m.

stories.title: Game #15 Preview & Open Thread: Buffalo Sabres vs Ottawa Senators
stories.summary:
Sabres look for fourth win in a row, donning new Hometown Remix threads



Puck Drop: 7:30 p.m. ET | KeyBank Center, Buffalo, N.Y.



TV: Prime, MSG-B

Know Your Opponent

Record: 9-6-1 | 19 points

Division Ranking: 3rd



PP: 30th, 12.5% [Sabres: 23rd, 17%]

Season Series: Sabres 2-1-1 vs. Ottawa in 2025-26 season



What to watch



California Dreamin’ 



The Buffalo Sabres are riding high, returning home after a near perfect four game road trip in which they went 3-0-1 against the Washington Capitals, San Jose Sharks, Anaheim Ducks, and Los Angeles Kings. While they weren’t perfect in every game, they found ways to get the job done when needed.



In more ways than hockey, California draws out the stars, and that was the case for the Sabres on their trip. Tage Thompson led the charge for the Sabres in what ended up a herculean trip for the Sabres’ best forward. Although he only had one point in the first two games of the trip. Thompson caught fire Thursday night in Anaheim, putting up a natural hat trick and recording five total points in the Sabres 7-6 win over the Ducks, then dazzled in his encore Saturday night in LA, recording two more goals in the Sabres’ 3-2 win. It shouldn’t be a coincidence that Thompson was reuinited with the players he consistently plays the best with in Zach Benson and Peyton Krebs.



Speaking of Benson, there has been a ton of discourse online about his expected impact, which has him near the elites of the NHL when it comes to play generation, versus his actual impact, which saw him goal-less heading into the trip. Benson too found more of his scoring touch, netting his first two of the season, while one of those two was an empty netter, he did more than enough on the play to fully earn it. 




Zach Benson picks Ivar Stenberg's pocket, puts the puck THROUGH the rookie's legs and puts away the empty netter 😮‍💨🚨 pic.twitter.com/EH0qNFX6S3— Gino Hard (@GinoHard_) October 28, 2026




Benson ended with seven total points on the four game trip, though it will be worth watching if he even plays tonight, and while he was out of practice on Monday, with Sabres’ coach Lindy Ruff listed him as day to day and he was back on the ice Tuesday. 



It wasn’t just the forwards who elevated their game though. Rasmus Dahlin has been through several ups and downs already to start this season, including a three game absence with a lower body injury. The Captain appears to have found his game, specifically Thursday night in Anaheim, where he recorded two points, was a +3, and had an 85xG% in what was a truly dominant effort by the captain. And while not as dominant in the expected stats against the Kings on Saturday, he did rack up two more assists, putting him at nine points in 11 games on the season. 




NHL Game Score Impact Card for Buffalo Sabres on 2026-10-29: pic.twitter.com/NZj7gEOkOI— HockeyStatCards (@hockeystatcards) October 30, 2026




Net Gains



Even with the hot streak, part of the story for the Sabres remains between the pipes. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen got the nod on Saturday against Washington, and finished about even in Goals Saved Above Expected in the 4-3 overtime loss. This was Luukkonen’s sixth game and fifth start in a row, in what has obviously been a less than ideal start for the Sabres’ goalie. 



Colten Ellis then got the start against the Sharks and recorded the Sabres’ first shutout of the season, finishing three goals saved above expected, locking in the best performance by a Sabres goalie this season. Ellis, in turn, got the next start against Anaheim, and gave back everything good he did against San Jose, finishing three goals saved below expected, almost melting down entirely, costing the Sabres the game allowing three goals in the final 10 minutes. To his credit in that game, the first three goals allowed all had some disastrous puck luck for the Sabres and Ellis, and he did make his fair share of saves in the first couple periods, and one huge one in the waning seconds of the third period to keep the Sabres ahead. 



We got the best and worst of Colten Chaos on the road trip, and it was enough chaos for Ruff to turn back to Luukkonen against the Kings, where he in turn rewarded the Sabres with his best performance of the season, finishing 1.43 goals saved above expected and stopping 27 out of the 29 shots he faced. 



The wrinkle in net grows as well, as Alex Lyon, who has yet to play this season, was back on the ice at practice on Monday, indicating he should be ready to go soon. FOr all that has been made of the struggles in net so far for the Sabres, not having Lyon healthy has been a huge detriment, as the stability he provides and the uncertainty that is Ellis never allowed Luukkonen or the Sabres to really work through his struggles like they did last year. If Lyon can even be 75% of the player he was last year for the Sabres, he’ll be a huge boon for the Sabres in net. It appears Ellis will get the net on Wednesday. 



Other Notes



Special Teams



The Sabres Power Play improved drastically on the trip, particularly in the games against Anaheim and Los Angeles, as they scored two power play goals in each game. Even against the Sharks and Capitals where the results didn’t go their way, their process with the man advantage certainly looks improved. The Sabres will need their power play to finally come alone, especially if their penalty kill remains as ineffective as it has been to start the season.



Injuries



Injuries were a bit of a theme of the trip, as both Konsta Helenius and Jiri Kulich were out of the lineup for the last couple games for the Sabres. Helenius took a big hit from Jacob Trouba against the Sharks and was flown back to Buffalo. Lindy Ruff said Monday he was considered week to week. Kulich, however, who also did not play the last two games of the trip, was back on the ice for practice on Monday. 



Lyon and Kulich were not the only Sabres to return to practice on Monday either, as both forward Justin Danforth and defenseman Connor Timmins were skating with the team again. Although Timmins couldn’t be described as a fan favorite, the Sabres might miss his contributions on the penalty kill, as the sixth defenseman spot for the team this year has been a relatively significant weakness in his wake, as both Zach Metsa and Dennis Gilbert have been quite sporadic. 



Hometown Remix



The Sabres will have a new look when they take the ice on Wednesday, in the form of the new Hometown Remix jerseys, which were formally announced on Monday.

stories.title: A Few Thoughts about the Ravens Game, in no particular order
stories.summary:
I'm going to start by saying that I really enjoyed this win. There's something satisfying about beating the Ravens, especially since I live here in enemy territory.  The morning radio today sounds liked a funeral.  And while the final score might suggest otherwise, I thought Baltimore's defense played a hell of a game, especially in the first half. They made us work for everything, consistently won the short-yardage battles, and forced Buffalo into some uncomfortable situations. That being said, the Bills didn't exactly help themselves. Between the turnovers, penalties, dropped passes, and some questionable play calling, the first half was much more difficult than it needed to be. Fortunately, the second half was a different story. The offense started making plays, the defense continued creating opportunities, and Buffalo eventually took control. I'm still trying to stick with my new approach of enjoying each game for what it is rather than immediately worrying about what everything means for January. So, with that in mind, let's enjoy a good win over a talented Ravens team, even if there were a few moments that made me want to throw something at my television.



	 



	1 - Josh - I thought this was an interesting game for Josh because there were moments where he looked absolutely incredible and others where he seemed just a little off. The play where he completely juked Buchanan out of his shoes was hilarious. I don't know how someone Josh's size can make defenders look that foolish in the open field. And of course, there's the Shnowplow touchdown, which continues to be one of the most unstoppable plays in football. But there were also some missed opportunities. On one third down, Josh had Shakir wide open underneath and Coleman running free downfield, but he missed Coleman on the deep throw. Later, he nearly threw an interception on a slant after the big DJ Moore catch. There were also several plays where nobody seemed to be open and Josh was left trying to make something happen. Still, I thought he settled in nicely as the game went on. The 40-yard completion to Kincaid was beautiful, and he eventually found Moore for the touchdown that moved him past Jim Kelly on the franchise passing touchdowns list. That's a pretty incredible accomplishment when you think about the amount of time Josh did it in. Then he hits Kincaid wide open for another touchdown later. Josh wasn't perfect, but he made the plays we needed and continues to rewrite the Bills record books. Pretty cool to be watching that happen in real time.



	 



	2 - Brady - I'm genuinely curious what Brady was seeing from Baltimore's defense because there were several stretches where I couldn't understand what we were trying to accomplish. We started the game using play action, which I liked, and had some success with the short passing game. But then we started getting cute in short-yardage situations, and that's where things got frustrating. We have one of the best short-yardage quarterbacks in football, yet on third and goal from the one, we run outside instead of using the Shnowplow. Earlier, we had that strange pitch to Cook on fourth and one that initially looked short before the review gave us the first down. Then there's another third-and-short situation where we call something unnecessarily complicated. Why? I understand that Baltimore has a very good defense, and maybe they were showing something that forced us to adjust. Maybe Brady was trying to put some new looks on film. But I personally believe in enforcing your will until the other team proves they can stop it. If the Shnowplow works, keep running it. If Cook is having success between the tackles, keep feeding him. Don't make things more complicated just because you can. And can someone explain throwing a three-yard pass to a double-covered Coleman on third and eight? I'm all for creativity, but sometimes the simplest answer is the right one.



	 



	3 - Geno Stone - How about Geno Stone?! I don't know if he was trying to prove something against his former team, but he certainly played like it. The sideline tackle where he came flying in like a missile was fantastic. Then he helps create the interception when the ball ricochets off him and into IGB's hands. I thought Stone brought a level of physicality and aggressiveness that was noticeable from the beginning of the game. He wasn't just making tackles; he was attacking the football and making things happen. That's exactly what I want to see from our safeties. And considering how well the defense played overall, I don't see any reason why he shouldn't be starting again next week. Sometimes a guy earns another opportunity simply by making the most of the one he's given. Stone did exactly that.



	 



	4 - You say the walls are closing in on you child
	All your friends have put you in exile
	Bad luck seems to follow you all around the world
	You can't seem to find no peace of mind girl
	You will take a chance to seem so bad



	 



	5 - The Defense - I thought this was one of the more encouraging defensive performances we've seen in a while. Yes, Baltimore was dealing with quarterback injuries, and that absolutely matters. But Buffalo still deserves credit for consistently getting pressure, forcing turnovers, and making life difficult for whoever was behind center.



	Bishop had a great strip sack that KEO recovered. Landon Jackson came up with a big sack near the goal line. Groot recorded his seventh sack and was disruptive throughout the second half, including making plays on consecutive downs to help force a three-and-out. Walker nearly had another strip sack, although the replay correctly overturned it. Benford almost had a pick-six on fourth down, and Dorian Williams recovered the botched snap late in the game. I also liked seeing the defense get more aggressive in certain situations. On a third and four in the second half, we brought pressure and forced an incompletion. That's the kind of thing I want to see more often. We had stretches where we were giving Baltimore too much room and not sending pressure, especially before halftime, but overall I thought the defense played well. I'm also curious about Jim Leonhard calling the game from the booth. I don't know how much of a difference that actually made, but I liked what I saw from the defense today.



	 



	6 - Bass - I don't think Bass is getting nearly enough credit for what he's doing right now. He drills a 56-yard field goal off the crossbar, setting a new Bills record for consecutive field goals made. Then he comes back and hits another one from 51 yards before halftime. Remember when every field goal attempt felt like a coin flip? I certainly do. There was a stretch where I almost dreaded seeing Bass walk onto the field. Now he's consistently making kicks from distances that used to make me nervous. And these weren't meaningless kicks. Buffalo was struggling offensively in the first half, and Bass kept putting points on the board when we couldn't finish drives. Those six points mattered, especially considering how well Baltimore's defense was playing. It's been great watching him regain his confidence. Hopefully this continues because having a reliable kicker can make an enormous difference when the games start getting tighter.



	 



	7 - Penalties - Holy crap, this was a sloppy game. Dawkins gets called for a false start on the opening drive. Hawes adds another false start and later gets called for holding. Cook commits a chop block that knocks us back 15 yards when we're already in field goal range. Oliver gets flagged for a low hit, and Bernard follows it up with another 15-yard penalty on the very next play. Now, I thought some of these calls were terrible. The Bernard penalty was particularly questionable, and Baltimore had a touchdown wiped out by a holding call that I thought was equally bad. There were questionable calls going both ways. But regardless of how you feel about the officiating, Buffalo committed too many mistakes that were completely within its control. The Cook penalty before halftime was especially frustrating because we had just gotten the ball back in excellent field position following the interception. Instead of having a relatively easy opportunity to add points, we immediately moved backward. Good teams are going to make enough plays against you without needing your help. We have to stop giving away yards and opportunities through unnecessary penalties.



	 



	8 - Short Yardage - I don't remember the last time I watched the Bills struggle this much in short-yardage situations. Baltimore's defensive front was absolutely winning those battles in the first half. Whether it was Cook getting stopped, the strange pitch play on fourth and one, or the inability to punch the ball in from the one-yard line, it felt like every yard was a fight.



	And I give Baltimore a lot of credit for that. Their defense was physical, disciplined, and clearly prepared to challenge us at the line of scrimmage. They weren't intimidated by Josh or our running game. But I still don't understand why we repeatedly moved away from the things we do best. The Shnowplow worked for the opening touchdown. Why not trust it again? Instead, we end up settling for a field goal after having third and goal from the one. I know teams are going to study that play and find ways to defend it, but until they consistently stop it, I'm not sure why we're the ones making the adjustment.



	 



	9 - Pass Catchers - I use that term lightly considering the drops we saw in this game.  Tight Ends not named Kincaid, and even Kincaid once, dropped some very catchable balls or batted them into the hands of the defenders.  Seriously Hawes, was your average of one false start a game not enough attention for you?  Moore looked good out there at times, but I do hope he didn't add another injury to the list with his ACL.  His jump ball bomb catch from Allen makes you wish he was on the team for the playoff game against the Broncos last year.  Shakir was great to start the game and I would say have an overall prototypical Shakir type of game.  Coleman should've had a nice long touchdown but Josh overthrew him (put some air under it next time).  Other than that, Coleman wasn't really a factor.  I'm starting to think Coleman and Moore struggle to exist on the field together along with Cook and Kincaid.  There were quite a few replays that showed all of the receivers blanketed in coverage, but we also saw some nicely drawn up plays with guys running open.  Either way, against a defense that was playing well to start, the receiving game was an improvement.  



	 



	10 - Bigger Picture - So here's where I'm allowing myself to look beyond this particular game. First, I'm happy. We beat the Ravens, the defense played well, Josh added another milestone to his ridiculous career, and we saw several players make important contributions. Geno Stone was excellent, Groot continued making plays, Bass was fantastic, and the offense eventually found its rhythm. There was a lot to like, especially in the second half. But I also can't ignore how sloppy we were before halftime. The turnovers, dropped passes, penalties, and questionable play calls made a game that we eventually controlled much more difficult than it needed to be. Baltimore's defense deserves a ton of credit, but Buffalo repeatedly got in its own way. That's what concerns me going forward. Against a team that's healthy at quarterback and capable of consistently moving the football, those mistakes could be the difference between winning and losing. We can't assume the defense is always going to create turnovers or that Josh will eventually bail us out. I also continue to wonder whether we're overthinking things offensively. We have an incredibly talented quarterback, one of the best running backs in football, and an offensive line that should be capable of imposing its will. I understand the desire to be unpredictable, but sometimes I think we're trying so hard to outsmart the other team that we end up outsmarting ourselves.



	Still, I'm going to stick with my promise to enjoy the individual games more. The Bills won, they played a much better second half, and there were some legitimately encouraging performances. I'll take that every week.



	 



	Go Bills!!!!

stories.title: Sabres scare up a California sweep behind Thompson, Luukkonen
stories.summary:
Buffalo’s power play strikes twice as Sabres beat Kings 3–2 and finish road trip with seven of eight points



Boxscore



Score: Buffalo Sabres 3–2 Los Angeles KingsShots: BUF 31–29 LAKPower Play: BUF 2-for-3; LAK 1-for-5Goaltending: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen — 27 saves on 29 shots (.931)



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Quinn 8 PPG (Benson, Dahlin), Thompson 9 (Benson, Samuelsson), Thompson 10 PPG (Quinn, Dahlin)



Los Angeles Kings Goals: Perry 1 PPG (Moore, Clarke), Lee 1 (Laughton, Armia)



Quick Thoughts



A power play with some bite



Buffalo wasted little time handing out its first Halloween treat. Jack Quinn opened the scoring at 6:35 of the first period, converting on the power play with assists from Zach Benson and Rasmus Dahlin. The Sabres carried a 12–6 shot advantage into the first intermission. Getting the early lead was welcome; getting it from the power play was another encouraging sign after Buffalo scored twice with the extra skater in Anaheim. That improvement would become the difference in the game. Buffalo finished 2-for-3, giving the Sabres four power-play goals on six opportunities over the final two games of the trip. Opposing penalty kills suddenly have a little more reason to be nervous.



The Kings provide the scare.



Tage Thompson extended Buffalo’s lead to 2–0 at 15:38 of the second period, with Benson and Mattias Samuelsson collecting the assists. Coming off a hat trick against the Ducks, Thompson clearly hadn’t lost his scoring touch in Anaheim. But Los Angeles wasn’t ready to turn off the porch lights. Corey Perry scored on the power play at 17:24, cutting Buffalo’s lead in half before the second intermission. Andre Lee then tied the game just 1:29 into the third. In less than six minutes of game time, the Sabres’ two-goal cushion had disappeared. The Kings outshot Buffalo 14–12 in the second and 9–7 in the third. The Sabres had to find a response while Los Angeles was generating more work for Luukkonen.



Thompson delivers another treat.



That response arrived after Mikey Anderson went to the penalty box for tripping at 13:29 of the third. Eleven seconds later, Thompson scored his second goal of the game, and Buffalo regained its lead. Quinn and Dahlin assisted on the power-play winner, which left the Sabres with 6:20 to protect a 3–2 advantage. Thompson finished with eight shots and reached 10 goals for the season. Five goals across the final two games of the trip is quite a souvenir from Southern California. Quinn contributed a goal and an assist, while Benson and Dahlin each finished with two helpers. Buffalo’s offensive leaders delivered when the game was winnable.



Luukkonen shuts the door.



Playing his 200th NHL game, Luukkonen stopped 27 of 29 shots and allowed nothing after Lee’s tying goal early in the third. His teammates helped absorb the pressure. Buffalo blocked 30 shots, including eight from Samuelsson. Owen Power led the team with 27:12 of ice time, while Samuelsson played 25:59. The penalty kill also did its part, finishing 4-for-5. That included a crucial late kill after Thompson was called for roughing at 16:21, giving the Kings another chance to erase Buffalo’s lead. There was plenty of time for one more Halloween fright. Luukkonen and the Sabres made sure it never arrived.



At The Horn



Three California stops, three wins, and seven of eight points from the full four-game road trip.



Buffalo won in different ways along the way. Colten Ellis supplied a shutout in San Jose, the offense carried a wild night in Anaheim, and the finale brought together productive special teams, strong goaltending, and a willingness to block shots.



The two-goal lead getting away remains something to clean up. But Buffalo answered that setback with a winning power-play goal and protected the advantage through a late penalty kill.



A power play finding its bite, Thompson filling the net, and Luukkonen finishing strong: that’s a Halloween haul worth bringing home.

stories.title: Game #14 Preview & Open Thread: Buffalo Sabres at Los Angeles Kings
stories.summary:
It’s Halloween Havoc as Sabres Shoot for Three Wins in a Row in L.A.



Buffalo Sabres (6-4-3) vs Los Angeles (4-6-2)



Puck Drop: 4:00 pm ET | Crypto.com Arena



TV: MSG-B, DAZN, ESPN+ (Hulu), NHL Center Ice

Know Your Opponent



Los Angeles Kings



Record: 4-6-2 | 10 PTS

Season Series: The Sabres were 2-0 last season against L.A. with a pair of 4-1 victories



What to Watch



1. Riding the Road Trip to Victory



Buffalo comes into today’s game against Los Angeles looking to sweep California. The Sabres shut down the Sharks 2-0 earlier in the week and survived the Ducks by a 7-6 margin on Thursday late night TV. Now they look to usurp the Kings and complete the trifecta on Halloween.



Tage Thompson and his line of Peyton Krebs and Zach Benson exploded against Anaheim on Thursday night. TNT collected three goals and five points, while Benny chipped in with a goal and two assists. Krebs rounded things out with three helpers of his own. This combo really clicked together, and I can’t imagine head coach Lindy Ruff won’t roll with that trio once again.



The Sabres have collected five of a possible six points on this road trip so far (including Washington) and have picked up points in four of their last five games overall. A win today would run the table on the Golden State and set Buffalo up nicely for a return to KeyBank Center next week. The Sabres will open a four-game homestand starting with the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday, November 4th.







2. Kings Improving After Being Put in Check Early



Los Angeles has scratched and clawed their way to three wins in their last five games after a miserable start to the season. Much like the Sabres in Anaheim, the Kings nearly suffered a complete meltdown on home ice against the Senators. After building a commanding 5-1 third-period lead, Los Angeles watched Ottawa storm back to tie the game. Fortunately for the Kings, Quinton Byfield came to the rescue, scoring the overtime winner just 1:23 into the extra frame to salvage the victory.



The 35-year-old Artemi Panarin has been pacing the Kings offensively so far this season, recording 8 goals and 13 points through 12 games. He’s showing no signs of slowing down, playing some of his best hockey despite his age. Meanwhile, 23-year-old Brandt Clarke is leading the way on the blue line. Clarke is a dynamic offensive defenseman, a premier puck-mover and power-play quarterback. Buffalo would be wise to keep these two players on their radar.



The Sabres (Atlantic) and Kings (Pacific) both sit in seventh place, despite Buffalo holding a fairly better early season record with 15 points compared to Los Angeles with 10. What a difference a division makes.







3. Whose Hot, Whose Not



Tage Thompson certainly qualifies as hot after his five-point outburst in Anaheim. Zach Benson has scored goals in back-to-back games while continuing to pile up the assists. And we can’t forget Jack “O’ Lantern” Quinn, who has recorded 10 points (5 goals, 5 assists) in his last 10 games for Buffalo.



The Sabres’ fourth line deserves some recognition here as well. Beck Malenstyn and Tyson Kozak, in particular, have been outstanding, bringing tight checking, physical play, shot blocking, and even chipping in offensively. According to Natural Stat Trick, with Malenstyn and Kozak together at 5-on-5 during the California trip, Buffalo holds an 8-2 advantage in high-danger scoring chances. That doesn’t even include Kozak’s goal on Thursday.



Sam Carrick returned after a four-game injury absence to join the duo, with spot duty from Krebs while mostly playing alongside Thompson.



Who is NOT hot is the Sabres’ penalty killers. After a brief reprieve over the last two games, the Ducks went absolutely ham on Buffalo with the man advantage. Anaheim finished 3-for-4 with the extra skater and made it look relatively easy. They also added two more goals with the goalie pulled in 6-on-5 situations.



The Blue and Gold have no answers for this right now, so my recommendation is simple: stay the hell out of the penalty box! Being down a man has become a real horror show for the Sabres.



News and Notes



Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen manned the starter’s net during Friday’s practice, suggesting he’ll get the nod against the Kings. It will be his first appearance since stealing a point for Buffalo against Washington.



Forward Noah Östlund, who scored a power-play goal in Anaheim, missed practice for maintenance reasons but is expected to play against Los Angeles.



Brandt Clarke was recently listed as day-to-day and his status is uncertain.

stories.summary:
Buffalo came from behind yet again, but have Ellis to thank for win



Boxscore



Score: Buffalo Sabres 7-6 Anaheim DucksShots: BUF 30-35 ANA



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Kozak 1 (Carrick, Samuelsson), Östlund 4 PPG (Benson, Thompson), Thompson 6 (Benson, Krebs), Thompson 7 (Krebs), Thompson 8 (Dahlin, Krebs), Quinn 7 PPG (Thompson, Dahlin), Benson 2 (Zellweger) Anaheim Ducks Goals: Granlund 3 PPG (LaCombe, Carlsson), Gauthier 3 PPG (Senecke, Carlsson), McQueen 1 (Colangelo, Jensen), Gauthier 4 PPG (LaCombe, Carlsson), Luneau 2 (Caulfield), Sennecke 8 (Unassisted). 



Quick Thoughts



O Defense, Defense, Wherefore Art Thou?



The Sabres penalty kill had gone two whole games without conceding a goal, but that streak came to a shuddering halt very early on in this game. Olen Zellweger was overexcited to see his former team and took a holding penalty just 35 seconds in. Then Zach Benson joined him in the penalty box for a tripping call and then the Ducks took advantage scoring on both the 5-on-3 then the ensuing 5-on-4 to go up by two less than three minutes into the game. 



That start would have rocked most goalies but fresh off his shutout in San Jose, Colten Ellis stayed on top of things even as his teammates remained in a stupor. He made close to half a dozen big saves including stopping a breakaway and a couple of odd-man rushes. How they were not down by four or five only Ellis knows and he’s not telling. 




Ellis save on Carlsson #LetsGoBuffalo #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/SkvinmbDSb— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 30, 2026




It’s not like the Sabres were overwhelmed by the hosts nor was Ville Husso giving up Yaroslav Askarov vibes, but they finally got back into the game thanks to the energetic fourth line paired up with captain Rasmus Dahlin and Mattias Samuelsson. Tyson Kozak’s shot from the blue line beat Husso shielded by Beck Malenstyn and it was 2-1 at the midpoint of the period. 




Tyson Kozak, 2-1 #LetsGoBuffalo #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/yStbeWhAxC— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 30, 2026




If you thought this would wake the Sabres up defensively, unfortunately it didn’t. Rookie Roger McQueen deflected a shot just past Ellis, it hit the backboards and before any of the Buffalo players could react McQueen had slammed the rebound past Ellis on the stick side, and the Ducks two-goal deficit was restored.



Now, what are the Sabres really, really familiar with this season? If you said being behind by two then you win yourself a piece of your kids’ Halloween candy, go get one right now. If you picked anything with no chocolate in it we are not talking anymore. 



Who didn’t get that memo? Apparently Joel Quenneville and his Ducky-boys because a minute after they scored their third Tyson Hinds tripped Josh Doan and to the power play the League’s most ineffective man-advantage unit went. The Sabres most consistent forward this season so far showed up big with Noah Östlund in the right place at the right time after Benson’s shot from the slot was blocked to make it 3-2, Buffalo’s first road power play goal of the season. 




Ostlund, 3-2 PPG #LetsGoBuffalo #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/rukEGLLq1N— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 30, 2026




Tage Thompson often threatens to take over games and he decided Anaheim were to be his shooting ducks tonight. Tommy Dangles took a feed from Benson at the blue line and drove towards the net, skirted a retreating Luneau and lifted the puck over Husso’s puck to make it 3-3 with over five minutes still left in the first stanza. 




Tage with a beauty, 3-3 #LetsGoBuffalo #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/VImG4x6HSQ— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 30, 2026




The remaining few minutes were relatively uneventful as the two teams went into the break level, Ducks led 12-9 in shots with a 13-8 edge in scoring chances. 



Sabres Doubly Redoubled



Buffalo have been one of the worst teams in the league in the second periods of games, but they came out from the locker room likely having been reminded of that by Lindy Ruff. 



Back and forth the two teams continued trading chances like they had in the first period, but once again the Sabres had Ellis to thank for his concentration as he made two big saves sprawled out in the paint. The Sabres then amped the ante as they poured on the shots with Anaheim powerless to keep them out of their zone. 




Ellis saves on Greer and Gauthier #LetsGoBuffalo #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/IgEZWS6cFp— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 30, 2026




On a two-on-one Jason Zucker found Ryan McLeod but he fluffed his chance, then Zucker was tripped into the boards and went down heavily with Buffalo going back to the power play, but were unable to take advantage. 




Zucker got taken out by a sliding McLeod.  Down on the ice as it cut to a commercial break #LetsGoBuffalo #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/cv168YPgwi— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 30, 2026




Anaheim had a few rare moments of second period control before Thompson decided to reprise his dominant self from the first period. Peyton Krebs won an offensive zone faceoff with the puck going straight back to the top of the circle where Tage waited on one knee and his wrister over the stick side beat Husso to give the Sabres their first lead of the night at the 18:36 elapsed mark. 




Tage Thompson right off a draw, 4-3 #LetsGoBuffalo #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/AKdZSlUmFP— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 30, 2026




Stunned, the Ducks lost the ensuing faceoff in the center circle to Krebs, who found Rasmus Dahlin on the left, and his cross-ice pass went to a streaking Thompson who cut in from the right. Having humbled Luneau on his first goal, he proceeded to embarrass Hinds with his blinding speed, and then tucked the puck neatly through Husso’s five-hole barely fifteen seconds after his second goal to earn his tenth hattrick. That put the Sabres up by two and was his tenth tripletta for Buffalo, bringing him level with Danny Gare and Alexander Mogilny. Rick Martin remains well ahead with 21 and Gilbert Perreault in second with 18. 




Tage Thompson HAT TRICK, 5-3 #LetsGoBuffalo #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/RoCWxwoGof— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 30, 2026




Winged by Tage, the Ducks were relieved to go into the locker room without giving up more goals. The Sabres dominated the shot count 15-5, and 14-5 in scoring chances. 



Buffalo kissed thee ere Buffalo killed thee



The third period has been the Sabres’ best period by far with a +10 differential as they looked to become the first team in the league to reach four wins from multi-goal comebacks, while the Ducks have been awful in the last stanza with a -7 scoring record. 



Early in the third the Sabres had two good scoring chances stopped by Husso before Dahlin was taken down, Sennecke with a lazy trip in the neutral zone for another Buffalo power play. Sabres got the bounces in San Jose, and that semeed to have carried to Anaheim, with Ostlund’s centering pass seeking Benson going off LaCombe’s skate and flying in past Husso, and just like that the Sabres had a second road power play goal after entering the game tonight with none so far, 6-3 the score. 




Jack Quinn has a pass go off Lacombe and in, 6-3 PPG #LetsGoBuffalo #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/mjI5bcMIrY— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 30, 2026




“Benson can’t finish”, “Benson’s shot sucks”, “Benson this” and “Benson that”.  About five minutes after the Sabres had taken the three-goal lead, they made it six straight goals scored with Benson racing onto a banked pass off the boards by Zellweger on his homecoming to slot home over Husso’s blocker, 7-3.




Zach Benson breakaway goal, 7-3 #LetsGoBuffalo #FlyTogether pic.twitter.com/Maui2t9ymU— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 30, 2026




Dennis Gilbert took an unnecessary interference penalty 6:49 in and the Sabres PK started strong with a Beck Malenstyn shooting chance on the kill, going 1-on-3. Ducks went straight back up the ice with Gauthier beating Ellis coming across to make it 7-4 with over half the period still to play. 



If the Sabres were ruffled they didn’t show it as they managed the clock without giving the Ducks too much life even as the crowd tried to pump their boys. Coach Q then pulled the goalie with 6:15 left and a three-goal deficit to make up for and the Ducks selling out to try to draw level. 



Power and Quinn both had long range shots go wide of the empty net for icing while Ellis continued to keep Anaheim at bay. Two and a half minutes into the 6-on-5 Kozak had a chance to score the empty-netter but his stick got tied up at the critical moment. 



Five minutes into the empty net situation and the Sabres had been happy to keep the Ducks at bay rather than trying to score another, but then with just over a minute left in the game, Luneau got a lucky bounce off a skate to make it 7-5 and the Ducks were attempting to mount a comeback. 



The Sabres then made a hash of clearing their zone with Anaheim buzzing and with thirty seconds left in the game Ellis’ clearance in front of him fell straight to Sennecke who gratefully made it 7-6, oh boy. 




COLTEN ELLIS WITH NO GLOVE SAVES THE SABRES ASSES FROM ONE OF THE WORST FALL APARTS EVER pic.twitter.com/3cfBaHRHII— Crossing Swords ⚔️ (@CrossSwordsPod) October 30, 2026




Ellis then had to sell out to make a crazy couple of kick saves as his catching glove went flying and the Sabres got an icing call to their benefit to end the game 7-6 with the Sabres having blown a four-goal lead in their favorite period, the third. The Ducks ended the period 16-6 on shots and 15-5 on scoring chances.  



At The Horn



This was an opposite game in many respects with the Sabres playing great in the second period but then mailing it in in the third where they have been so good. Colten Ellis was incredible at times in this game, both keeping the Ducks out in the first when they led two-nothing, and then at the end when they poured it on 6-on-5.  



River hockey was at its finest tonight and the Sabres might get away with playing this style with Ellis in goal and possibly even Alex Lyon, but they certainly cannot give up this high a volume of shots with Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen between the pipes. Ruff will not be pleased with how this one ended, but a win is a win and the Sabres now have two regulation wins out of two on this West Coast swing so far. 




NHL Game Score Impact Card for Buffalo Sabres on 2026-10-29: pic.twitter.com/NZj7gEOkOI— HockeyStatCards (@hockeystatcards) October 30, 2026

Buffalo looks to stay hot out west



Buffalo Sabres (5-4-3) at Anaheim Ducks (5-6-1)



Puck Drop: 10 p.m. ET | Honda Center, Anaheim, Calif.



TV: ESPN+, Disney+, HuluNOTE: This is an ESPN+ exclusive national game and will not be broadcast on MSG-B.

Know Your Opponent



Anaheim Ducks



Record: 5-6-1 | 11 PTS



Last Game: 6-5 OT loss vs Vancouver



Division Ranking: 5th



PP: 9th, 23.7% [Sabres: 32nd, 9.8%]



PK: 19th, 77.6% [Sabres: 25th, 71.4%]



Season Series: Sabres 1-0-1 vs. Ducks in 2025-26 season



What to Watch



1. Can the new third line stay hot?



The Sabres have been desperately searching for better offensive balance among their forward lines, and it resulted in a shakeup that broke up the reliable Benson-Ostlund-Quinn trio for Tuesday’s win over San Jose.



With new combos galore, the line of Jason Zucker, Josh Norris and Ryan McLeod was by far the most dominant versus the Sharks — likely to the surprise of many Sabres fans.



The Zucker-Norris-McLeod line out-chanced the Sharks 13-4 and finished with an 83.3 xGF% at five-on-five. If Buffalo can get that consistent level of production from their middle six every night, it would go a long way.



2. Zellweger revenge game



Olen Zellweger will face his former team for the first time on Thursday, and with the form he’s in, the 23-year-old might have the Ducks second guessing their decision to trade him.



Zellweger leads Sabres defensemen this season in xGF% at 57.7% and tallied the eventual game-winning goal against San Jose, his third of the season to go with two assists. His pairing alongside Owen Power has been one of the strongest not just on the Sabres, but in the NHL.



There isn’t a more fitting opponent than the Ducks for Zellweger to continue his strong start to the season against.



3. Lame Ducks



It’s been a tough go as of late for Anaheim.



The Ducks have lost six of their last seven games, and allowed at least four goals in five of those losses. Arguably the worst of those was their last game against lowly Vancouver, in which Anaheim blew a 5-2 third period lead to lose in overtime, 6-5.



In that same seven-game span, they have a 41.8 xGF% at five-on-five play, while the team’s goaltenders, Lukas Dostal and Ville Husso, have combined for a .862 save percentage.



If the Sabres can play a five-on-five game similar to what they did against San Jose, they should be in great position to make it two wins in two on their California trip.



4. Ellis in net again



Lindy Ruff is riding the hot hand in net, as Colten Ellis is set to get his second start in a row on Thursday.



Ellis was stellar in Tuesday’s win over San Jose, stopping all 23 shots he faced to go with 2.73 goals saved above expected, according to HockeyStats.com. It was an even more impressive game considering it was his first action in 15 days.



With the Sabres’ goaltending situation facing plenty of question marks at the moment, this start feels like a fantastic opportunity for Ellis to secure some more looks in the near future, and potentially, a longer-term starting role.



Injury Notes



The Sabres suffered a tough blow when it was announced Thursday that forward Konsta Helenius suffered an upper-body injury against San Jose and returned to Buffalo for further evaluation. Buffalo will also be without forward Jiri Kulich, who remains in concussion protocol. Sam Carrick will slot into the lineup as he returns from a middle-body injury.



Anaheim placed defenseman Pavel Mintyukov on injured reserve last week with a lower-body injury, and he will not play against Buffalo. The Ducks continue to be without forwards Troy Terry (hip) and Ryan Poehling (knee), as well.

Colten Chaos Dazzles as Sabres blank Sharks, 2-0
stories.summary:
Score: Buffalo Sabres 2, San Jose Sharks 0



Shots: Buffalo 40 – 23 San Jose 



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Zellweger (3) (Helenius, Power); Benson (1) (Thompson, Power)



San Jose Sharks Goals: N/A



Summary



In spite of a lofty shot total and a bevy of scoring chances, the Buffalo Sabres blanked the San Jose Sharks by a score of 2-0 on Tuesday night. Colten Ellis was the story of the game, stopping 24 shots for his second career shutout and the team’s first of the season. Olen Zellweger gave the Sabres the 1-0 lead early in the second, and Zach Benson gave them the insurance marker with an empty netter in the final minute of the game.



High Octane First



The game got off to a sloppy, low pace start as the game saw a few stoppages early on, including Louis Crevier flipping the puck over the glass to give the Sharks a power play just 1:30 into the period. The Sharks, however, would give that penalty right back as Josh Norris found himself on a breakaway, drawing a slashing penalty to go back to 4-4 hockey. 




JOSH NORRIS?!?!?!?! pic.twitter.com/0s5mxJeYSG— Crossing Swords ⚔️ (@CrossSwordsPod) October 28, 2026




Macklin Celebrini made his presence felt early, generating high quality chances that the Sharks were unable to convert, including picking Rasmus Dahlin’s pocket a couple times. Celebrini got the best of the Sabres’ captain a couple times early, though nothing found its way past Colten Ellis. 




Rasmus????? pic.twitter.com/lqiPrYrMqL— Crossing Swords ⚔️ (@CrossSwordsPod) October 28, 2026




Then the Sabres got cooking a bit, thanks to the line of Norris, Ryan McLeod, and Jason Zucker. That group got several nice opportunities on Yaraslov Askarov, including Zucker trying to bank it in off the Sharks’ goalie. The defensemen for the Sabres got involved as well, as Dahlin and Mattias Samuelsson found themselves on a 2-1, with Dahlin feeding a pass to Samuelsson that was shot just wide.



Those two continued to create chances, as Dahlin dangled around old friend Michael Kesselring, bringing the puck to the wall and finding Samuelsson in the slot, generating yet another quality chance that Askarov had to stop. 




Dahlin used the booty to throw a reverse check on Gaudette #LetsGoBuffalo #SJSharks pic.twitter.com/TcCd2Bj5XY— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 28, 2026




The Sabres continued to dictate pace, getting many good looks but were unable to finish, which is a growing trend for the team this season. The Sharks would get another look on the power play, however, as Crevier found himself in the box again, this time on a questionable call fighting for position by the net. The Sharks were able to get several good looks on the man advantage, highlighted by Ellis having to make a huge blocker save on a shot wide open in the slot to keep the game scoreless in the waning minutes of the first period. 



The revamped lines for the Sabres were all firing in the first, as with a few minutes left, Konsta Helenius and Tage Thompson combined for an excellent chance, as Dahlin and Helenius played pitch and catch at the blue line, leading to Helenius taking the puck behind the net finding a wide open Thompson between the circles. Askarov made the save and dove for the rebound, but every Sabres line generated something strong in the first period. The lines have been one of the biggest stories 11 games into the season, as they have changed in effectively every game so far this season, but this first period probably featured the best hockey the forward group has collectively played all season. 




Ellis save on Gaudette #LetsGoBuffalo #SJSharks pic.twitter.com/avTLfrMN9t— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 28, 2026




The Sharks wouldn’t stay quiet for long though, as we got a classic “Colten Chaos” sequence with the Sabres goaltender making several high leverage saves as the Celebrini line got to work again in the Sabres zone. The Sabres withstood another late flurry, with Celebrini getting another golden opportunity that Ellis was able to stop, this time from the left circle.




Östlund stops this one from going in pic.twitter.com/1ReGQVSRpX— Crossing Swords ⚔️ (@CrossSwordsPod) October 28, 2026




The period ended 0-0, but not for lack of trying. The Sabres outshot the Sharks 16-12, and 28 combined shots is the most in an NHL period this season to result in no goals. The Sabres held an xG edge of 1.39-1.26 after the first period. 



Second Period Chaos



The Sabres translated that high energy first period into early success in the second. Just 50 seconds into the period, Helenius found Olen Zellweger on an odd man rush, and Zellweger ripped a shot through Askarov to give the Sabres a 1-0 lead. It was Zellweger’s third goal of the season, and a nice impression for Helenius getting to play between Thompson and Zach Benson. Owen Power picked up the second assist, as he started the breakout from the defensive zone. 




Olen Zellweger, 1-0 #LetsGoBuffalo #SJSharks pic.twitter.com/AGPuKBa6CD— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 28, 2026




If not for Askarov, however, the Sabres would have found themselves a couple goals up. The Sharks were struggling to generate much of anything for the first half of the second period, while the Sabres remained all over. McLeod found Zucker for a shot in the slot that Askarov kept out, while the rebound bounced out to Crevier, who was robbed by a scrambling Askarov to keep it 1-0 with 13 minutes left in the second. 



The Sharks did finally generate a sequence of glorious chances, once again kept out on a Colten Chaos sequence. A shot made its way past Ellis off the stick of Michael Misa, but it hit old friend Michael Kesselring in the shin and deflected wide, leading to a full on scramble drill where Ellis was able to find the puck and cover it. 




Chaos around the Sabres net! #LetsGoBuffalo #SJSharks pic.twitter.com/Fb8Th9RPrh— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 28, 2026




Ellis made another tremendous save mere moments later, robbing a cross ice pass from Celebrini to Colin Graf with the left pad to keep it 1-0. Helenius also blocked a shot off the rebound, once again providing Ellis some help to maintain the lead. 




Ellis save on Graf 👀#LetsGoBuffalo #SJSharks pic.twitter.com/maaYG4ptVZ— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 28, 2026




With eight minutes left, the Sabres found themselves with their first real power play opportunity on the night as Dahlin took a high stick. Zach Benson still remains one of the most snake bitten players in the league, as on that power play, he had a redirection off a Dahlin shot stopped, then had a glorious chance right in front of the net that did not find its way in. The Sabres, though unable to convert, did put up a pretty good showing on the man advantage, though we are wearing thin on power play moral victories.



The Sabres continued to dominate possession and shot attempts for effectively the rest of the period, but the Sharks did find themselves with a late power play, as Benson went to the box for holding with 21 seconds remaining in the second period. The Sharks held possession for that full 21 seconds, but thanks to a huge shot block by Josh Norris, were unable to get anything on Ellis. The Sabres actually were able to hold a lead heading into the third period, by that same score of 1-0. They held an edge in shots on goal 30-17, and held the xG edge, 2.41-2.09. 




WHAT A WAY TO LAY OUT THE BODIES TO KEEP IT SCORELESS THROUGH TWO pic.twitter.com/LM4blerioM— Crossing Swords ⚔️ (@CrossSwordsPod) October 28, 2026




Stout Third Period



The Sharks did start the third period with a pretty lengthy power play opportunity after the penalty late in the second period, though the Sabres penalty kill was once again stout, not allowing the Sharks to get too much with the man advantage. 



With 17:11 remaining in the game, the Sabres would get another power play opportunity of their own, as Thompson came soaring up the wing, too quickly for Adam Gaudette to handle cleanly, being forced to hold him to prevent a greater chance. While the firs extended power play for the Sabres featured several chances, the second one was more of the same old Sabres, being largely ineffective and unable to set up. 




The beautiful game (and ugly Sabres power play) pic.twitter.com/TwCwVOeMjZ— Crossing Swords ⚔️ (@CrossSwordsPod) October 28, 2026




Immediately after the man advantage expired for the Sabres, the Sharks once again found themselves with a flurry of glroius scoring chances but once again Ellis was somehow able to keep them all out of the net, even losing his stick on this sequence. 



The Sharks made repeated pushes to try and break through, but the Sabres defense held pretty firm, not allowing much in the way of Ellis in the middle part of the period, and what did get to Ellis was knocked down. The line of Zucker-Norris-McLeod combined for their best chance of the third period, requiring an excellent pad save by Askarov to make a save on Zucker on a cross-ice feed from Norris. 



Ellis was tested again with four minutes left, as a shot from Kesselring took a bad bounce off the glass and popped right back out in front to Kiefer Sherwood, who was all alone in front of Ellis, but he whiffed on the shot and stuck it right into Ellis, holding the score at 1-0 still in the dying minutes. 




Ellis save on Sherwood #LetsGoBuffalo #SJSharks pic.twitter.com/GjrpNOrdZL— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 28, 2026




Askarov was then tasked with keeping the deficit at one, and he once again delivered, denying Noah Ostlund on a cross ice one timer with just 2:30 left in the game. 



The Sabres fended off an empty net push from the Sharks, keeping everything outside, until Tage Thompson flipped a puck out to center ice where Zach Benson went to work. He took Ivar Stenburg to the wall, turned him around, outmuscled him to the puck and got it to open in front, and with a heroic lunge, poked it into the empty net for his first goal of the season, securing a win for the Sabres. This was the team’s 40th shot of the contest. 




Stenberg wasn't prepared for Zach Benson. 2-0 ENG #LetsGoBuffalo #SJSharks pic.twitter.com/QFYsOAGGF4— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) October 28, 2026




Ellis secured the Sabres’ first shutout of the season, stopping all 24 Sharks shots, including some highlight reel saves. This was the second career shutout for Ellis. 



Wrap Up



The Sabres had an interesting reversal of a trend that has plagued them all season, as three of the four forward lines were quite impactful, while the Doan-Ostlund-Quinn line was the one that wasn’t quite holding up their end of the bargain. It is probably not a coincidence that line struggled without Benson, and Thompson and Helenius were really good with Benson.



There will defintely be a question of what to do in net for the Sabres, as you have to imagine Ellis gets the next start. He was tremendous for the Sabres on Tuesday night (Wednesday morning?), giving the team by far the best performance they’ve had in net this season. 



Much has been made of Ryan McLeod’s struggles to start the season, and while he did not record a point in this game, his performance took a huge leap playing next to Jason Zucker, who have made an excellent duo for their entire tenure in blue and gold. Those two, along with Norris, were the Sabres three leaders in xG% in the victory against the Sharks. 



In only their third opportunity of the season to hold a lead in the third period, the Sabres did an excellent job. The Sharks had just seven shots in the third period, and mustered 0.7 xG in the period despite trailing the entire time. The team simply kept their foot on the gas and were rewarded for their efforts. 



What’s Next



The Sabres remain on the west coast, as they will take on the Anaheim Ducks on Thursday night at 10 p.m.
